name: Question 5
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/71f160891f01681b485b2eb88dccf63b05271fab8e24f069e3bab46f4168c454.png)

Evaluate ${∬}_{D}6x\,dA,$ where $D$ is the region shown in the picture above.
worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/bb95d1507eb1cd527b6d6983cc0531d71c3852db002f188f220954a367de8d95.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,-\sqrt{y+2}\le x\le -\sqrt{2-y}}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,2\le y\le 3,\,-\sqrt{y+2}\le x\le 0}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}6x\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}6x\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}6x\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-\sqrt{y+2}}^{-\sqrt{2-y}}6x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{-\sqrt{y+2}}^{0}6x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}\,{|}_{-\sqrt{y+2}}^{-\sqrt{2-y}}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{3}3{x}^{2}\,{|}_{-\sqrt{y+2}}^{0}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3[{(-\sqrt{2-y})}^{2}-{(-\sqrt{y+2})}^{2}]\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{3}3[{0}^{2}-{(-\sqrt{y+2})}^{2}]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3(-2y)\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{3}3(-y-2)\text{d}y \\  & =-3{\int }_{0}^{2}2y\,\text{d}y-3{\int }_{2}^{3}(y+2)\text{d}y \\  & =-3{y}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{2}-3(\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+2y){|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =-3(2)^{2}-3(\frac{{3}^{2}}{2}+2(3))+3(\frac{{2}^{2}}{2}+2(2)) \\  & =-12-\frac{63}{2}+18 \\  & =-\frac{51}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
